messages:
anne: quick sync — i want to resolve how the gateway should handle in-flight streaming requests when model routing changes (e.g., variant A->B fallback or capacity failover). current behavior is awkward: we either cancel and force client retry or try to resume but risk duplicate tokens. thoughts?

kai: +1 this keeps biting us on long responses. What invariants do we want? single-response exactly-once vs progress-preserving best-effort?

anne: goal is: avoid user-visible duplicates, preserve partial progress on cheap fallbacks, and keep memory bounded at edge. ideally a resume token API that lets the next backend continue from a safe checkpoint.

maria: how small/large are checkpoints? if we checkpoint every N tokens we add latency and state. we need a memory model: best-effort prefix cache in gateway + KV of small resume tokens pointing to cached KV state on serving nodes.

jordan: agree. proposal: attach a short-lived lease token to each stream. lease carries: model-id, sequence-offset, idempotency-hash, and preferred-fallback-path. gateway keeps slight buffer (e.g., last 4 chunks) and hands off token on retry. backend can request the buffer from gateway during resume.

leon: that sounds good. question: how do we avoid replay/duplicate output if both backends produce the same continuation? need a deterministic merge rule. maybe backends must return a `skip_prefix_bytes` value when resuming.

anne: exactly — on resume backend returns the number of bytes/tokens to drop relative to what's already been delivered. gateway enforces dedupe by dropping anything before that offset. We must standardize units (tokens vs bytes). prefer token offsets.

kai: sample handshake (proto-ish):

```
Client -> Gateway: start_stream { model: redwood-3b, idempotency_key: K }
Gateway -> BackendA: open_stream { lease: L1 }
...streaming chunks...
Gateway (failover) -> BackendB: resume_stream { lease: L1, checkpoint_token: T }
BackendB -> Gateway: resumed { applied_offset_tokens: 120 }
Gateway: drop first 120 tokens from buffer, continue sending
```

maria: buffering policy: gateway only buffers up to X tokens per stream (configurable, default 256 tokens), if exceed -> fail fast and instruct client to retry from idempotency_keyfull-resume (i.e., server-side replay).

jordan: backpressure: we already expose per-stream window. on resume, BackendB must advertise its available token window before sending to avoid head-of-line blocking. also need a retry budget to cap how many mid-flight switches allowed.

leon: observability: emit events: lease_created, lease_transferred, resume_attempt, resume_success/failure, dedupe_applied. include trace-id and sample payload size. we should log applied_offset_tokens to catch regressions.

anne: corner case: model variant mismatch (A vs B semantics differ). we should only allow resume across compatible variants (same tokenizer + compatible stopping behavior). gateway should validate model-compatibility via model-catalog metadata before attempting resume.

kai: security: lease tokens must be opaque, short-lived, HMAC-signed by gateway (no customer data inside). if a backend can't verify HMAC, reject resume.

maria: performance note: maintaining per-stream buffers increases mem pressure. recommend a global buffer pool with eviction based on smallest progress-first. and predictable per-node caps.

jordan: operational: add canary that enables resume for a subset of traffic + synthetic prompts to assert correctness (no dupes, latency within SLO).

leon: :thumbsup: i can sketch telemetry dashboard: resume rate, success %, avg applied_offset, memory/stream count per edge node.

anne: next steps: kai + maria draft a minimal API (lease token fields + resume RPC) and a small impl plan (buffer limits, compatibility checks). jordan + leon will define SLO/telemetry requirements. i'll file an RFC follow-up with that workplan.

sre-bot: deploy notice: edge-config v2.14 rolled out to canary cluster at 2026-03-20T15:22:00Z — monitor resume-related alerts for 2h.

kai: will do. thanks everyone.
